records.source: Ἔλεγεν δὲ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς πρὸς τὸ δεῖν πάντοτε προσεύχεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ μὴ ἐγκακεῖν, λέγων· Κριτής τις ἦν ἔν τινι πόλει τὸν θεὸν μὴ φοβούμενος καὶ ἄνθρωπον μὴ ἐντρεπόμενος.
records.gloss: He was speaking then a parable to them about the [need] for them always to pray and not to lose heart, \v 2 saying, A certain judge there was in a certain city, God not fearing and man not respecting.
pieces: Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart.
He said, "There was once a judge in a certain city who did not fear God and had no regard for anyone.

L.1: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was telling them a parable about their need always to pray and not to lose heart,
L.2: saying, "In a certain city there was a certain judge who did not fear God and did not respect {{gender:people|man}}.

R.1: Jesus told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples a story. He wanted to teach them that they should always pray and never give up hope.
R.2: He said, "In a certain town there was a judge. He had no fear of God, and he did not care about people.

decisions.choice: about their need always to pray: Luke states the point of the parable before it is told
alternatives: a title for the story only
decisions.reason: Luke tells the reader in advance what the parable teaches: to keep on praying and not give up while waiting for God to act (18:7-8).

decisions.choice: lose heart: become discouraged and give up
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow weary or lose courage (2 Corinthians 4:1, 16).

decisions.choice: did not fear God and did not respect people: answerable to no one
decisions.reason: To fear God and respect people was the mark of a just judge (2 Chronicles 19:6-7). This judge cared for neither.

decisions.choice: his disciples
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" are; Jesus has been speaking to the disciples since 17:22.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:5
alternatives: a quotation for each part of the story
decisions.reason: The parable is one speech; the Lord's comment in 18:6 starts a new one.

records.heading: A widow who kept coming

records.source: χήρα δὲ ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσα· Ἐκδίκησόν με ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου μου.
records.gloss: A widow then there was in the city that, and she was coming to him saying, Avenge me of the adversary of me.
pieces: In that city there was also a widow who came to him again and again. She said, 'Give me my rights against my opponent.'

L.3: And there was a widow in that city, and she kept coming to him, saying, 'Give me justice against my adversary.'

R.3: In that town there was also a widow. She kept coming to the judge and saying, 'Someone is treating me unfairly. Please judge my case and give me justice.'

decisions.choice: a widow: a woman with no husband to support or defend her
decisions.reason: A widow often had no one to speak for her in court. The law commanded special care for widows (Exodus 22:22; Deuteronomy 10:18), and the prophets condemned judges who ignored them (Isaiah 1:23).

decisions.choice: give me justice: decide my case in my favor and make it right
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to avenge, but in a court case it means to see that justice is done for someone who has been wronged.

decisions.choice: she kept coming: again and again
decisions.reason: The tense shows repeated action, which is the point of the story.

decisions.choice: Someone is treating me unfairly. Please judge my case
alternatives: Give me justice against my adversary
decisions.reason: Readable explains what kind of help she asked for.

records.source: καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἐπὶ χρόνον, μετὰ ταῦτα δὲ εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ· Εἰ καὶ τὸν θεὸν οὐ φοβοῦμαι οὐδὲ ἄνθρωπον ἐντρέπομαι, διά γε τὸ παρέχειν μοι κόπον τὴν χήραν ταύτην ἐκδικήσω αὐτήν ἵνα μὴ εἰς τέλος ἐρχομένη ὑπωπιάζῃ με.
records.gloss: And not he would for a time; afterward however he said within himself, If even God not I fear nor man respect, \v 5 because yet causes me trouble the widow this, I will avenge her, so that not to the end coming she exhaust me.
pieces: For a while he refused. But later he said to himself, 'I do not fear God and I have no regard for anyone.
Still, this widow is such a nuisance that I will give her justice. If I do not, she will keep coming until she wears me out.'"

L.4: And for a time he was not willing; but afterward he said within himself, 'Even though I do not fear God nor respect {{gender:people|man}},
L.5: yet because this widow causes me trouble, I will give her justice, so that she does not keep coming and in the end wear me out.'"

R.4: For a while the judge refused to help her. But at last he said to himself, 'I do not fear God, and I do not care about people.
R.5: But this widow keeps bothering me. So I will make sure she gets justice. If I do not, she will keep coming back and wear me out!'"

decisions.choice: wear me out: exhaust me with her pestering
decisions.reason: The verb first meant to strike under the eye, as a boxer does (1 Corinthians 9:27). Here it is probably used loosely, of being worn down; the judge is tired, not afraid of being hit. Some take it to mean that she will damage his reputation.

decisions.choice: to the end coming: by coming on and on, or coming at last
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "in the end" or "continually". Either way, the judge gives in because she will not stop.

decisions.choice: he said within himself: the judge's motive is his own comfort
alternatives: he came to care about her
decisions.reason: The judge does not change his character. Even a man like this gives in to persistence; the next verses argue from the lesser to the greater (18:7).

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: The narrator speaks in 18:6.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος· Ἀκούσατε τί ὁ κριτὴς τῆς ἀδικίας λέγει·
records.gloss: Said then the Lord, Hear what the judge of unrighteousness says;
pieces: The Lord said, "Listen to what the unjust judge says.

L.6: And the Lord said, "Hear what the unrighteous judge says.

R.6: Then the Lord Jesus said, "Listen to what this unfair judge says.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Luke the narrator calls Jesus by his title
the judge of unrighteousness: the unjust judge
alternatives: a judge who rules on unrighteousness
decisions.reason: The Hebrew way of describing someone by a noun ("of unrighteousness") means a judge marked by injustice (16:8).

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable adds the name, as in 12:42.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:8
decisions.reason: The Lord's comment on the parable is one speech.

records.source: ὁ δὲ θεὸς οὐ μὴ ποιήσῃ τὴν ἐκδίκησιν τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ τῶν βοώντων αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, καὶ μακροθυμεῖ ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς;
records.gloss: And God not not shall execute the avenging of the elect of him, the [ones] crying out to him day and night, and is he delaying over them?
pieces: Then surely God will give justice to the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen, when they call out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} day and night. Will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} be slow to help them?

L.7: And will not God bring about justice for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen ones, who cry out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} day and night? And will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delay over them?

R.7: God will surely see that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen people get justice. They cry out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} day and night. Will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keep them waiting?

decisions.choice: will not God bring about justice: a question expecting a strong "yes"
decisions.reason: The double negative expects "Yes, of course he will". If an unjust judge gives in, how much more will God, who is just and loves his people.

decisions.choice: his chosen ones: the people God has chosen as his own
alternatives: a small group of special believers
decisions.reason: Israel was God's chosen people (Isaiah 65:9); the word is used of all who belong to God (Romans 8:33).

decisions.choice: and will he delay over them: a second question, expecting "no"
alternatives: though he is patient with them
and he is patient with them
decisions.reason: The verb means to be patient or to be slow to act. Its sense here is debated. Taken as a question, it expects that God will not put them off; others read it as a statement that God is patient. 18:8 says he will act quickly.

decisions.choice: a statement: surely God will
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the expected answer as a statement.

records.source: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ποιήσει τὴν ἐκδίκησιν αὐτῶν ἐν τάχει.
records.gloss: I say to you that he will execute the avenging of them in quickness.
pieces: I tell you, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will see them vindicated, and without delay.

L.8: I tell you that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring about justice for them quickly.

R.8: I tell you, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give them justice, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do it quickly.

decisions.choice: quickly: soon, or suddenly when the time comes
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean soon or swiftly. Jesus has just spoken of days of waiting (17:22), so the point may be that when God acts he will not hold back.

decisions.choice: bring about justice: put right what has been done to them
decisions.reason: The same word as in 18:3, 5.

decisions.choice: see them vindicated
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a word for being shown to be in the right.

records.source: πλὴν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐλθὼν ἆρα εὑρήσει τὴν πίστιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς;
records.gloss: Nevertheless the Son of Man having come, indeed will he find the faith on the earth?
pieces: Even so, when the Son of Man comes, will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} find this kind of faith on the earth?"

L.8: Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} find faith on the earth?"

R.8: But when the Son of Man comes, will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} find anyone on earth who still has faith?"

decisions.choice: faith: the faith that keeps praying and does not give up, like the widow's
alternatives: the Christian faith as a body of teaching
decisions.reason: The word has the article, "the faith", which points back to the kind of faith the parable has shown (18:1).

decisions.choice: will he find: a question that warns, without giving the answer
alternatives: a prediction that no one will have faith
decisions.reason: The particle leaves the answer open and turns the question on the hearers.

decisions.choice: this kind of faith (B); anyone ... who still has faith (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the article's point, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: Εἶπεν δὲ καὶ πρός τινας τοὺς πεποιθότας ἐφ’ ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι εἰσὶν δίκαιοι καὶ ἐξουθενοῦντας τοὺς λοιποὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην·
records.gloss: He spoke now also to some trusting in themselves that they are righteous and despising the others the parable this.
pieces: There were some who relied on themselves, sure that they were righteous, and who looked down on all others. Jesus told them this parable.

L.9: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and looked down on everyone else.

R.9: Some people felt sure that they were good and right with God, and they thought they were better than everyone else. Jesus told them this story.

decisions.choice: righteous: in the right before God
decisions.reason: The word means just, upright, and so accepted by God. These people trusted their own goodness to make them right with God (16:15).

decisions.choice: looked down on: treated as nothing
decisions.reason: The verb means to count as worthless (23:11).

decisions.choice: good and right with God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as the meaning decision does.

decisions.choice: the people described first, then the parable
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the hearers in one sentence and introduce the parable in another.

records.source: Ἄνθρωποι δύο ἀνέβησαν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν προσεύξασθαι, ὁ εἷς Φαρισαῖος καὶ ὁ ἕτερος τελώνης.
records.gloss: Men two went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
pieces: "Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.

L.10: "Two men went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.

R.10: "Two men went up to the temple courts to pray. One of them was a Pharisee. The other was a man who collected taxes.

decisions.choice: a Pharisee: a member of a Jewish movement devoted to keeping the law of Moses strictly
decisions.reason: As explained at 5:17 and 17:20. Pharisees were respected by the people for their devotion.

decisions.choice: a tax collector: a Jew who collected taxes for the Romans or their rulers
decisions.reason: As at 3:12 and 5:27. Tax collectors were despised as collaborators and cheats.

decisions.choice: went up into the temple: the temple stood on a hill in Jerusalem
alternatives: went up into the sanctuary building
decisions.reason: People went up to the temple and down from it (18:14). Prayer was offered there at the times of the morning and evening sacrifices (Acts 3:1). The word is the temple with its courts, not the sanctuary building.

decisions.choice: the temple courts
decisions.reason: Readable shows that they prayed in the courts, not inside the building.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:14
alternatives: no quotation marks for the parable
decisions.reason: Jesus tells the parable and comments on it in one speech.

records.source: ὁ Φαρισαῖος σταθεὶς πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ταῦτα προσηύχετο· Ὁ θεός, εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ὥσπερ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἅρπαγες, ἄδικοι, μοιχοί, ἢ καὶ ὡς οὗτος ὁ τελώνης·
records.gloss: The Pharisee having stood toward himself thus was praying, God, I thank you that not I am like the rest of the men, swindlers, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector;
pieces: The Pharisee stood and prayed this prayer about himself: 'God, I thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that I am not like the rest of humanity, who are swindlers, crooks and adulterers, or even like this tax collector.

L.11: The Pharisee, standing, was praying these things toward himself: 'God, I thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that I am not like the rest of {{gender:people|men}}, swindlers, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.

R.11: The Pharisee stood up and prayed about himself. He said, 'God, thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that I am not like other people. They rob others, they do evil, and they are not faithful in marriage. Thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that I am not like this tax collector either.

decisions.choice: toward himself: he prayed about himself, or to himself
alternatives: standing by himself, apart from others
decisions.reason: The phrase can go with "praying" (he prayed to himself, or about himself) or with "standing" (he stood by himself). Either way the prayer is centered on himself: "I" comes again and again.

decisions.choice: swindlers, unrighteous, adulterers: people who rob, who do wrong, who are unfaithful in marriage
decisions.reason: The first word means grasping people who take from others. The second means wrongdoers in general.

decisions.choice: I thank you: thanks used as a way to list his own merits
decisions.reason: Thanking God was right (Psalm 100:4), but this prayer asks for nothing and compares himself with others.

decisions.choice: Thank you that I am not like this tax collector either.
alternatives: or even like this tax collector
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the thanks to keep the sentences short.

decisions.choice: the prayer is in single quotation marks inside the parable and runs to 18:12
decisions.reason: The Pharisee's words are quoted inside Jesus' speech.

records.source: νηστεύω δὶς τοῦ σαββάτου, ἀποδεκατῶ πάντα ὅσα κτῶμαι.
records.gloss: I fast twice in the week, I tithe all things as many as I gain.
pieces: Twice every week I fast, and I give a tenth of everything I take in.'

L.12: I fast twice in the week; I give a tenth of all that I gain.'

R.12: I go without food two days every week. And I give a tenth of all the money I get.'

decisions.choice: I fast twice a week: going beyond what the law required
decisions.reason: The law of Moses commanded fasting only on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29). Devout Jews of the time also fasted twice a week, on Mondays and Thursdays.

decisions.choice: I give a tenth of all I gain: the tithe, on everything, not only what the law named
alternatives: a tenth of his profit only
decisions.reason: The law required a tenth of the crops and herds (Deuteronomy 14:22-23). The Pharisees were careful to tithe even small herbs (11:42). This man tithes all he acquires.

decisions.choice: go without food; all the money I get
decisions.reason: Readable explains fasting and puts "gain" in everyday words.

records.source: ὁ δὲ τελώνης μακρόθεν ἑστὼς οὐκ ἤθελεν οὐδὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἐπᾶραι εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, ἀλλ’ ἔτυπτε τὸ στῆθος αὐτοῦ λέγων· Ὁ θεός, ἱλάσθητί μοι τῷ ἁμαρτωλῷ.
records.gloss: But the tax collector afar off standing not was willing not even the eyes to lift up to heaven, but was striking the breast of himself saying, God, be merciful to me the sinner.
pieces: The tax collector, though, kept back at a distance and would not even lift his eyes toward heaven. Instead he struck his chest again and again and said, 'God, be merciful to me, the sinner!'

L.13: But the tax collector, standing far off, was not willing even to lift up [his] eyes to heaven, but was striking his breast, saying, 'God, be merciful to me, the sinner.'

R.13: But the tax collector stood far away. He did not even look up toward heaven. He kept beating on his chest in sorrow. He said, 'God, be merciful to me. I am a sinner!'

decisions.choice: be merciful to me: turn your anger away from me and show me mercy
alternatives: have pity on me in general
decisions.reason: This verb is not the usual word for mercy. It is used for God being turned from anger and making peace through the removing of sin (Hebrews 2:17 uses it of atoning for sins). In the temple, at the hour of sacrifice, the man asks God to deal with his sin and accept him.

decisions.choice: the sinner: he sees himself as the sinner, with no one to compare himself to
decisions.reason: The article points to himself alone. Where the Pharisee compared himself with others, the tax collector does not.

decisions.choice: striking his breast: a sign of grief and sorrow for sin
decisions.reason: People beat their chests in deep grief (23:48).

decisions.choice: standing far off, eyes down: shame before God
decisions.reason: People usually prayed standing, looking up toward heaven. He keeps his distance and his eyes down, like Ezra in Ezra 9:6.

decisions.choice: I am a sinner!
decisions.reason: Readable makes the description a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: in sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gesture meant.

records.source: λέγω ὑμῖν, κατέβη οὗτος δεδικαιωμένος εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ παρ’ ἐκεῖνον· ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται, ὁ δὲ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.
records.gloss: I say to you, went down this one justified to the house of him rather than that one; for everyone exalting himself will be humbled, the [one] however humbling himself will be exalted.
pieces: I tell you, it was this man, not the other, who went home put right with God. For everyone who lifts {{gender:themselves|himself}} up will be brought low, and the one who takes the low place will be lifted up."

L.14: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than that one. For everyone who exalts {{gender:themselves|himself}} will be humbled, but the one who humbles {{gender:themselves|himself}} will be exalted."

R.14: I tell you, when the two men went home, God had accepted the tax collector as right with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but not the Pharisee. Anyone who puts {{gender:themselves|himself}} above others will be brought down. But anyone who is humble will be lifted up."

decisions.choice: justified: declared right with God, accepted by him
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a judge's ruling that someone is in the right. God accepted the man who confessed his sin, not the one who listed his good deeds (compare Romans 4:5).

decisions.choice: rather than that one: the other was not justified
decisions.reason: The phrase does not mean both were justified to different degrees; it means this one and not the other.

decisions.choice: whoever exalts himself will be humbled: God reverses human rank
decisions.reason: Jesus said the same at a meal (14:11). The passives point to God, who brings down the proud and lifts up the lowly (1:52).

decisions.choice: put right with God (B); God had accepted ... as right with him (R)
decisions.reason: "Justified" is church language. Balanced and Readable say what it means; Literal keeps the word.

decisions.choice: brought low ... lifted up (B); brought down ... lifted up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the picture of going down and up.

records.source: Προσέφερον δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ τὰ βρέφη ἵνα αὐτῶν ἅπτηται· ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: They were bringing then to him also the infants, that them he might touch; having seen however the disciples were rebuking them.
pieces: People were even bringing their babies to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would touch them. The disciples saw it and began to scold them.

L.15: And they were bringing even the infants to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might touch them; but the disciples, having seen [it], were rebuking them.

R.15: People were bringing even their babies to Jesus. They wanted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to touch them. But when the disciples saw this, they told the people to stop.

decisions.choice: infants: babies
decisions.reason: The word means a newborn or very young child. In 18:16 Jesus calls them little children.

decisions.choice: touch them: lay hands on them in blessing
decisions.reason: Parents brought children to a teacher to be blessed with his touch (compare Mark 10:16; Genesis 48:14).

decisions.choice: were rebuking them: those who brought the children
decisions.reason: The disciples spoke sternly to the people bringing the children, perhaps thinking Jesus had more important work.

decisions.choice: told the people to stop
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the disciples spoke to and what they said.

records.heading: Children and the kingdom

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσεκαλέσατο αὐτὰ λέγων· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με καὶ μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: But Jesus called them to [him] saying, Permit the little children to come to me and not do forbid them, for of such is the kingdom of God.
pieces: But Jesus called them over and said, "Let the little children come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and do not try to stop them. The kingdom of God belongs to those who are like them.

L.16: But Jesus called them to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], saying, "Allow the little children to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and do not forbid them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

R.16: But Jesus called for the children to come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said, "Let the children come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! Do not keep them away. The kingdom of God belongs to people who are like them.

decisions.choice: called them: the babies, brought to him by those carrying them
decisions.reason: The word "them" refers back to the infants of 18:15.

decisions.choice: of such is the kingdom of God: the kingdom belongs to people like these
alternatives: the kingdom is made up only of children
decisions.reason: Children had nothing to offer and no standing. The kingdom belongs to those who, like them, come with nothing in their hands.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:17
decisions.reason: Jesus' words in 18:16-17 are one saying.

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you, whoever not shall receive the kingdom of God as a child, no not shall enter into it.
pieces: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not welcome the kingdom of God the way a child does will never get into it."

L.17: Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter into it."

R.17: I tell you the truth, you must accept the kingdom of God the way a child does. If you do not, you will never enter it."

decisions.choice: like a child: as a child receives it
decisions.reason: The words could mean receiving the kingdom as one welcomes a child, but the context is about being like children (18:16). A child receives what is given, with trust.

decisions.choice: will never enter: the strongest form of denial
alternatives: will find it hard to enter
decisions.reason: The double negative makes the statement emphatic.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: Luke's usual rendering of Jesus' "amen" (4:24).

decisions.choice: two sentences, addressed to "you"
decisions.reason: Readable puts the condition as a direct instruction.

records.source: Καὶ ἐπηρώτησέν τις αὐτὸν ἄρχων λέγων· Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;
records.gloss: And asked a certain him ruler saying, Teacher good, what having done life eternal will I inherit?
pieces: One of the leaders asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Good Teacher, what do I have to do to inherit eternal life?"

L.18: And a certain ruler asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Good Teacher, by doing what will I inherit eternal life?"

R.18: An important leader asked Jesus, "Good Teacher, what must I do to have eternal life?"

decisions.choice: ruler: a leader, perhaps of a synagogue or of the Jewish council
decisions.reason: The word is used for leaders of a synagogue (8:41) and members of the council (23:13). Luke does not say which. He is rich (18:23), and Matthew 19:20 says he was young.

decisions.choice: Good Teacher: a respectful, even flattering, form of address
alternatives: a statement that Jesus is God
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers were not usually addressed as "good". Jesus' reply (18:19) takes up the word.

decisions.choice: inherit eternal life: receive the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: As in 10:25. Eternal life is the life of the age to come (Daniel 12:2; 18:30).

decisions.choice: have
decisions.reason: As in 10:25: Readable uses a simpler verb; the meaning decision explains "inherit".

records.heading: A rich leader's question

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν;
records.gloss: Said then to him Jesus, Why me call you good?
pieces: Jesus answered, "Why are you calling {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} good?

L.19: And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} good?

R.19: Jesus said to him, "Why do you say that I am good?

decisions.choice: why do you call me good: Jesus makes the man think about what he has said
alternatives: Jesus denies that he is good
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say he is not good. He turns the man's attention to God, the only one who is good, and leaves him to ask what it means to call Jesus good.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:20
decisions.reason: Jesus' reply runs on without a break.

records.source: οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός.
records.gloss: No one [is] good except one, God.
pieces: No one is good but God alone.

L.19: No one [is] good except one: God.

R.19: Only God is good. No one else is.

decisions.choice: except one, God: an echo of Israel's confession that God is one
decisions.reason: The words recall Deuteronomy 6:4, "the LORD is one". Goodness in the full sense belongs to God (Psalm 106:1).

decisions.choice: God alone
decisions.reason: The word "one" here means only one; Balanced says "alone".

decisions.choice: Only God is good.
alternatives: No one is good except God
decisions.reason: Readable states the positive first.

records.source: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας· Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς, Μὴ φονεύσῃς, Μὴ κλέψῃς, Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα.
records.gloss: The commandments you know: Not you shall commit adultery, not you shall murder, not you shall steal, not you shall bear false witness, honor the father of you and the mother.
pieces: You know the commandments: 'Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not give false testimony. Honor your father and your mother.'"

L.20: You know the commandments: 'Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.'"

R.20: You know what God's commandments say: 'Do not be unfaithful in marriage. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not lie about others in court. Honor your father and mother.'"

decisions.choice: the commandments: from the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes the commandments about one's neighbor from Exodus 20:12-16 and Deuteronomy 5:16-20. Adultery comes before murder, as in some Greek copies of the Old Testament and in Romans 13:9. He does not quote the commandment against coveting, or the commands about God, which the next verses test (18:22).

decisions.choice: bear false witness: give false evidence against someone
decisions.reason: The commandment is about testimony in court (Deuteronomy 19:16-19), though it came to stand for all lying about others.

decisions.choice: do not commit adultery ...: prohibitions
decisions.reason: The form gives commands.

decisions.choice: be unfaithful in marriage; lie about others in court
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two less familiar terms.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks inside Jesus' words; the speech closes here
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes the law inside his speech.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ταῦτα πάντα ἐφύλαξα ἐκ νεότητος μου.
records.gloss: And he said, These all have I kept from [the] youth.
pieces: The man replied, "I have kept every one of these from my youth."

L.21: And he said, "All these I have kept from [my] youth."

R.21: The man said, "I have obeyed all these commandments since I was young."

decisions.choice: kept: obeyed, guarded
decisions.reason: The verb means to guard or keep a command. The man means he has lived by them.

decisions.choice: from youth: since he became responsible for keeping the law
decisions.reason: A Jewish boy was taught the law from childhood and held responsible for keeping it as he grew up.

decisions.choice: The man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

records.source: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἔτι ἕν σοι λείπει· πάντα ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ διάδος πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.
records.gloss: Having heard then Jesus said to him, Yet one thing to you is lacking; all as much as you have sell and distribute to [the] poor, and you will have treasure in [the] heavens, and come follow me.
pieces: Hearing this, Jesus told him, "You are still missing one thing. Sell all your possessions and hand out the money to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven. After that, come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.22: And having heard [this], Jesus said to him, "One thing is still lacking for you: sell all that you have and distribute [it] to [the] poor, and you will have treasure in [the] heavens; and come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.22: When Jesus heard this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "There is one more thing you need to do. Sell everything you own. Give the money to poor people. Then you will have treasure in heaven. After that, come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: one thing is lacking: the man's wealth stands between him and God
alternatives: he must do one more good deed to earn life
decisions.reason: Jesus puts his finger on what the man cannot give up. Following Jesus, not one more deed, is what he lacks (14:33).

decisions.choice: treasure in heaven: riches kept by God, which cannot be lost
decisions.reason: As in 12:33-34. What is given away for God is not lost.

decisions.choice: come, follow me: become my disciple
alternatives: walk behind me for a while
decisions.reason: To follow Jesus is to leave other things and go with him as a disciple (5:11; 9:23).

decisions.choice: hand out the money (B); give the money (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what is given.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας ταῦτα περίλυπος ἐγενήθη, ἦν γὰρ πλούσιος σφόδρα.
records.gloss: And having heard these things very sorrowful he became, he was for rich extremely.
pieces: At these words the man was filled with sorrow, for he was a man of great wealth.

L.23: But having heard these things, he became very sorrowful, for he was extremely rich.

R.23: When the man heard this, he became very sad. He was very rich.

decisions.choice: for: his wealth is the reason for his sorrow
decisions.reason: Luke explains the man's grief: he had much to give up.

decisions.choice: very sorrowful: deeply grieved
decisions.reason: The word means overwhelmed with grief.

records.source: Ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσπορεύονται·
records.gloss: Having seen then him Jesus said, How difficultly those riches having into the kingdom of God enter;
pieces: Seeing this, Jesus said, "What a hard thing it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!

L.24: And Jesus, having seen him, said, "How hard it is for those who have riches to enter into the kingdom of God!

R.24: Jesus saw how sad the man was. He said, "It is very hard for rich people to enter the kingdom of God!

decisions.choice: having seen him: without "become very sorrowful"
alternatives: having seen that he had become very sorrowful
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add that Jesus saw he had become very sorrowful, repeating 18:23. Some early manuscripts, including Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, do not have the words, and the SBLGNT follows them. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: how hard it is: riches make it hard to depend on God
decisions.reason: Wealth gives a sense of security that keeps people from depending on God (12:15-21; 16:13). Jesus says it is hard, and 18:27 shows that God can do it.

decisions.choice: how sad the man was
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus saw, from 18:23.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:25
decisions.reason: Jesus' words in 18:24-25 are one saying.

records.source: εὐκοπώτερον γάρ ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τρήματος βελόνης εἰσελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν.
records.gloss: Easier for it is a camel through an eye of a needle to go than a rich man into the kingdom of God to enter.
pieces: In fact, a camel could get through the eye of a needle more easily than a rich person could get into the kingdom of God."

L.25: For it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich [person] to enter into the kingdom of God."

R.25: It would be easier for a camel to go through the tiny hole in a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."

decisions.choice: a camel through the eye of a needle: something impossible
alternatives: a narrow gate in a city wall
a rope instead of a camel
decisions.reason: The camel was the largest animal in the land and the eye of a needle the smallest opening. The picture is a deliberate exaggeration; the hearers understood it as impossible (18:26). Nothing in the text supports the idea of a gate called "the eye of a needle".

decisions.choice: needle: a sewing or surgeon's needle
decisions.reason: Luke uses the word for a needle used in medicine, but the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the tiny hole in
decisions.reason: Readable explains the eye of a needle.

records.source: Εἶπαν δὲ οἱ ἀκούσαντες· Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι;
records.gloss: Said then those having heard, Then who is able to be saved?
pieces: Those listening asked, "Then who can be saved?"

L.26: And those who heard said, "Then who is able to be saved?"

R.26: The people who heard this asked, "Then who can be saved?"

decisions.choice: be saved: receive eternal life and enter the kingdom
decisions.reason: Here "saved" means the same as inheriting eternal life (18:18) and entering the kingdom of God (18:24-25).

decisions.choice: then who can be saved: many took riches as a sign of God's favor
decisions.reason: Scripture speaks of wealth as a blessing from God (Deuteronomy 28:1-14). If even the rich, whom God seemed to favor, cannot enter, then who can?

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Τὰ ἀδύνατα παρὰ ἀνθρώποις δυνατὰ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ ἐστιν.
records.gloss: But he said, The things impossible with men possible with God are.
pieces: He answered, "What human beings cannot do is possible for God."

L.27: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "The things impossible with {{gender:people|men}} are possible with God."

R.27: Jesus answered, "Some things are impossible for people, but they are possible for God."

decisions.choice: impossible with people, possible with God
decisions.reason: The words echo the angel's words to Mary (1:37) and the LORD's question to Abraham (Genesis 18:14). Salvation is God's work, not human work.

decisions.choice: men: human beings
decisions.reason: The word means people in general.

decisions.choice: What human beings cannot do
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the saying in natural order.

records.source: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφέντες τὰ ἴδια ἠκολουθήσαμέν σοι.
records.gloss: Said then Peter, Behold we having left the own things followed you.
pieces: Peter said, "But we have given up what was ours and followed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

L.28: And Peter said, "Look, we have left our own [things] and followed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.28: Then Peter said, "We left our homes and everything we had so that we could follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: our own things: our homes and all we had
decisions.reason: The phrase means one's own possessions, or one's home (John 19:27). Peter and the others had left their boats and homes (5:11).

decisions.choice: we: Peter sets the disciples beside the rich man
decisions.reason: The pronoun is emphatic. The disciples have done what the ruler would not do.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: our homes and everything we had
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase, as the meaning decision does.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδείς ἐστιν ὃς ἀφῆκεν οἰκίαν ἢ γυναῖκα ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ γονεῖς ἢ τέκνα ἕνεκεν τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ, ὃς οὐχὶ μὴ ἀπολάβῃ πολλαπλασίονα ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
records.gloss: And he said to them, Truly I say to you that no one there is who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God, \v 30 who not not shall receive manifold more in the time this, and in the age that coming life eternal.
pieces: He answered them, "Truly I tell you, anyone who has left a house, a wife, brothers, parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
is sure to be given back far more in this life, and in the age that is coming, eternal life."

L.29: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Truly I tell you that there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
L.30: who will not receive many times more in this time, and in the age that is coming, eternal life."

R.29: Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth. Anyone who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the kingdom of God
R.30: will get back much more in this life. And in the age that is coming, that person will have eternal life."

decisions.choice: many times more: far more than what was given up
decisions.reason: Jesus does not name a number. The new family of God's people more than makes up for what is left (8:21).

decisions.choice: this time ... the age to come: the present age and the age God will bring in
alternatives: two periods of a person's life
decisions.reason: Jewish teaching spoke of this age and the age to come. Eternal life is the life of the age to come, which the ruler asked about (18:18).

decisions.choice: brothers: brothers, and perhaps brothers and sisters
decisions.reason: The plural can include sisters; the list here is given from the point of view of a man who leaves a wife.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: Luke's usual rendering of Jesus' "amen" (4:24).

decisions.choice: anyone who has left ... will get back
alternatives: there is no one who has left ... who will not receive
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the double negative into a plain statement with the same meaning.

records.source: Παραλαβὼν δὲ τοὺς δώδεκα εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, καὶ τελεσθήσεται πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα διὰ τῶν προφητῶν τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
records.gloss: Having taken aside then the Twelve he said to them, Behold we go up to Jerusalem, and will be accomplished all things having been written through the prophets about the Son of Man;
pieces: Taking the Twelve aside, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them, "We are now going up to Jerusalem, and all that the prophets wrote about the Son of Man will come to pass.

L.31: And taking the Twelve aside, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything that has been written through the prophets about the Son of Man will be accomplished.

R.31: Jesus took the twelve apostles aside and said to them, "We are now going up to Jerusalem. There everything the prophets wrote about the Son of Man will happen.

decisions.choice: everything written through the prophets will be accomplished
alternatives: the prophets predicted only his death
decisions.reason: Jesus' suffering and rising fulfill what God said through the prophets (24:25-27, 44-46). The passive points to God's plan.

decisions.choice: about the Son of Man: what was written of him, or what will be done to him
alternatives: written by the Son of Man
decisions.reason: The phrase can go with "written" or with "accomplished". The sense is the same: Scripture is fulfilled in what happens to him.

decisions.choice: going up to Jerusalem: Jerusalem stands high in the hills
decisions.reason: From Jericho (18:35) the road climbs steeply up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: There
decisions.reason: Readable says where these things will happen.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:33
decisions.reason: Jesus' words in 18:31-33 are one speech.

records.heading: Going up to Jerusalem

records.source: παραδοθήσεται γὰρ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ ἐμπαιχθήσεται καὶ ὑβρισθήσεται καὶ ἐμπτυσθήσεται, καὶ μαστιγώσαντες ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ ἀναστήσεται.
records.gloss: He will be betrayed for to the Gentiles and will be mocked and will be insulted and will be spit upon, \v 33 and having flogged they will kill him, and on the day the third he will rise again.
pieces: He will be given over to the Gentiles, who will make fun of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, treat {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} shamefully and spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
After whipping {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} they will put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death, and on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise."

L.32: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be handed over to the Gentiles, and will be mocked and insulted and spat upon,
L.33: and having flogged [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], they will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise again."

R.32: He will be handed over to people who are not Jews. They will laugh at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, insult {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.33: They will beat {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with whips and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come back to life."

decisions.choice: handed over: given into the power of others
decisions.reason: As in 9:44: the verb is used for Judas' betrayal (22:4) and for the leaders handing Jesus to Pilate (23:1; 24:20).

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the nations other than Israel, here the Romans
decisions.reason: This is the first time in Luke that Jesus says the Gentiles will put him to death. Roman soldiers mocked and crucified him (23:33, 36).

decisions.choice: mocked, insulted, spat upon
decisions.reason: The words recall the servant of the Lord in Isaiah 50:6, who gave his back to those who beat him and did not hide his face from spitting.

decisions.choice: flogged: whipped with a scourge
decisions.reason: The Romans flogged prisoners with leather whips, often before crucifixion.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: Luke speaks in 18:34.

records.source: καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐδὲν τούτων συνῆκαν, καὶ ἦν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο κεκρυμμένον ἀπ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐκ ἐγίνωσκον τὰ λεγόμενα.
records.gloss: And they none of these things understood, and was the word this hidden from them, and neither they knew the things being spoken.
pieces: But the Twelve understood none of this. What {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said was hidden from them, and they did not grasp what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant.

L.34: And they understood none of these things, and this saying was hidden from them, and they did not know the things being said.

R.34: But the apostles did not understand any of this. The meaning of these words was hidden from them. They had no idea what Jesus meant.

decisions.choice: was hidden: its meaning was kept from them for a time
decisions.reason: As in 9:45. Only after the resurrection were their minds opened (24:45).

decisions.choice: three statements of one fact
decisions.reason: Luke says three times that they did not understand, to stress how far they were from seeing it.

decisions.choice: the Twelve (B); the apostles (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who did not understand.

records.source: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἐγγίζειν αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰεριχὼ τυφλός τις ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἐπαιτῶν.
records.gloss: It came to pass then in the drawing near of him to Jericho a blind [man] certain was sitting beside the road begging.
pieces: Jesus was approaching Jericho. A blind man was sitting there beside the road, begging.

L.35: And it happened, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drew near to Jericho, [that] a certain blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.

R.35: Jesus was coming near the city of Jericho. A blind man was sitting by the side of the road. He was begging people for money.

decisions.choice: Jericho: an old city near the Jordan, about a day's walk from Jerusalem
alternatives: the Jericho of Joshua's time only
decisions.reason: The road from Jericho climbed up to Jerusalem (10:30). Pilgrims to the Passover passed this way, so it was a good place to beg.

decisions.choice: begging: asking for gifts to live on
decisions.reason: A blind man had no other way to earn a living. Giving to the poor was a duty in Jewish life.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

records.heading: A blind man at Jericho sees

records.source: ἀκούσας δὲ ὄχλου διαπορευομένου ἐπυνθάνετο τί εἴη τοῦτο·
records.gloss: Having heard now a crowd passing along, he was asking what might be this.
pieces: He heard a crowd passing by and asked what it was all about.

L.36: And hearing a crowd passing by, he was asking what this might be.

R.36: He heard a crowd of people going by. He asked what was going on.

decisions.choice: he was asking: he kept asking
decisions.reason: The tense suggests he asked more than once, or asked those around him.

records.source: ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος παρέρχεται.
records.gloss: They told then him, Jesus the Nazarene is passing by.
pieces: They told him, "Jesus of Nazareth is going by."

L.37: And they reported to him, "Jesus the Nazarene is passing by."

R.37: People told him, "Jesus from Nazareth is going by."

decisions.choice: the Nazarene: the man from Nazareth
alternatives: a member of a religious group
decisions.reason: The word identifies Jesus by his hometown (4:16).

decisions.choice: they told him: given as their words
decisions.reason: The Greek introduces the words with a particle that can mark either a quotation or reported speech. All levels quote them.

decisions.choice: of Nazareth (B); from Nazareth (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the town.

records.source: καὶ ἐβόησεν λέγων· Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.
records.gloss: And he called out saying, Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.
pieces: So he shouted, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"

L.38: And he called out, saying, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"

R.38: So he shouted, "Jesus, Son of David, please have mercy on me!"

decisions.choice: Son of David: the King God promised from David's family, the Messiah
alternatives: a descendant of David by birth only
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose kingdom would last forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16; Isaiah 11:1-10). The angel said God would give Jesus David's throne (1:32). The blind man calls Jesus by this title, which the crowd only called "Jesus the Nazarene".

decisions.choice: have mercy on me: take pity on me and help me
decisions.reason: As in 17:13. He asks the King to act with kindness.

records.source: καὶ οἱ προάγοντες ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ ἵνα σιγήσῃ· αὐτὸς δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν· Υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.
records.gloss: And those going before were rebuking him that he should be silent; he however much more kept crying out, Son of David, have mercy on me.
pieces: The people at the front of the crowd told him sternly to be quiet, but he cried out all the louder, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"

L.39: And those going ahead were rebuking him, that he should be silent; but he kept crying out much more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"

R.39: The people walking in front told him to be quiet. But he shouted even louder, "Son of David, please have mercy on me!"

decisions.choice: those going ahead: the people at the head of the procession
decisions.reason: Luke does not say who they were. They walked in front of Jesus.

decisions.choice: kept crying out: shouted again and again
decisions.reason: The verb is a stronger word for shouting than in 18:38, and the tense shows he kept on.

decisions.choice: told him sternly
decisions.reason: Balanced says how they spoke to him.

records.source: σταθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ἀχθῆναι πρὸς αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Having stopped then Jesus commanded him to be brought to him.
pieces: Jesus stood still and gave orders for them to bring the man to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.40: And Jesus stood still and commanded him to be brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.40: Jesus stopped. He told the people to bring the blind man to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: commanded him to be brought: Jesus ordered those near him
alternatives: Jesus commanded the blind man to come
decisions.reason: The passive leaves unnamed who brought the man; it was the people around.

decisions.choice: the man (B); the blind man (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear which "him" is meant.

records.source: ἐγγίσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν·
records.gloss: Having drawn near then he, he asked him,
pieces: When the man came near, Jesus asked him,

L.40: And when he had come near, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked him,

R.40: When the man came close, Jesus asked him,

decisions.choice: he drew near ... he asked: the blind man came near, and Jesus asked
decisions.reason: The first "he" is the blind man, the second is Jesus.

decisions.choice: the man ... Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name both people.

records.source: Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω;
records.gloss: What to you do you want I shall do?
pieces: "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

L.41: "What do you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

R.41: "What do you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

decisions.choice: what do you want me to do for you: Jesus invites the man to say what he asks
decisions.reason: Jesus can see that the man is blind. He asks him to put his request and his trust into words.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Κύριε, ἵνα ἀναβλέψω.
records.gloss: And he said, Lord, that I might receive sight.
pieces: He answered, "Lord, I want to see again."

L.41: And he said, "Lord, that I may receive sight."

R.41: The man answered, "Lord, I want to be able to see again."

decisions.choice: Lord: a title of respect, here given to the Son of David
decisions.reason: The word can be a polite "sir", but this man has called Jesus the Son of David (18:38-39).

decisions.choice: receive sight: see again, or see
alternatives: see for the first time only
decisions.reason: The verb means to look up, and so to regain sight. It may mean he had once seen.

decisions.choice: I want to see again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the request as a natural sentence.

records.source: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀνάβλεψον· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.
records.gloss: And Jesus said to him, Receive sight; the faith of you has healed you.
pieces: Jesus told him, "See again. Your faith has made you well."

L.42: And Jesus said to him, "Receive your sight; your faith has saved you."

R.42: Jesus said to him, "Then see! Your faith has made you well and saved you."

decisions.choice: has saved you: has made you well, and more than that, has rescued you
decisions.reason: The verb means to save or rescue, and in healings to make well. Luke uses the same words for the woman whose sins were forgiven (7:50), the woman healed by touching Jesus (8:48), and the Samaritan (17:19). The man goes on to follow Jesus (18:43).

decisions.choice: your faith: his trust that Jesus, the Son of David, could and would heal him
decisions.reason: His faith showed in his cry and in his refusal to be silenced.

decisions.choice: receive sight: a command that heals
decisions.reason: Jesus heals by his word.

decisions.choice: made you well (B); made you well and saved you (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:48 and 17:19: Literal keeps "saved", Balanced says what happened to his body, and Readable uses both words.

records.source: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνέβλεψεν, καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ δοξάζων τὸν θεόν.
records.gloss: And immediately he received sight, and began following him glorifying God.
pieces: At once he could see, and he followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, giving glory to God.

L.43: And immediately he received sight, and began following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, glorifying God.

R.43: Right away the man could see again. He followed Jesus, giving glory to God.

decisions.choice: following him: going with Jesus, as a disciple does
decisions.reason: Unlike the rich ruler (18:22-23), the man who has nothing follows Jesus at once.

decisions.choice: glorifying God: praising God for what he had done
decisions.reason: As in 5:25 and 17:15.

records.source: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἰδὼν ἔδωκεν αἶνον τῷ θεῷ.
records.gloss: And all the people, having seen [it], gave praise to God.
pieces: All the people saw what happened, and they gave praise to God.

L.43: And all the people, having seen [it], gave praise to God.

R.43: All the people who saw this praised God too.

decisions.choice: the people: the crowd, God's people
decisions.reason: Luke often uses this word for the crowds of Israel who heard Jesus gladly (7:16; 19:48).

decisions.choice: praise: words of praise
decisions.reason: This is a different word from "glorifying" in 18:43a, a plain word for praise.
